Kuvitus: omenapuu kesäillan hämärässä ni: Illustration: an apple tree in a meadow on a summer evening at dusk. One apple has come loose from a branch and is halfway to the ground; motion lines trail behind it. In the sky, to the right of the tree, a full moon is shining.
Kaavakuva, ei mittakaavassa: vasemmalla: Diagram, not to scale: on the left the Earth, on the right an apple. The Earth pulls the apple with a force F1 that points from the apple towards the Earth, and the apple pulls the Earth with a force F2 of equal magnitude that points from the centre of the Earth towards the apple. The arrows are equally long. The acceleration of the apple is 9.8 metres per second squared, the acceleration of the Earth about 3 times 10 to the power minus 25 metres per second squared.
Kaavakuva: kaksi palloa, vasemmalla suur: Diagram: two spheres, a larger mass m1 on the left and a smaller mass m2 on the right. The distance r between the centres of the spheres is marked with a dimension line below the spheres. An equal gravitational force acts on each sphere towards the other sphere: F1 from the left sphere towards the right and F2 from the right sphere towards the left.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: vaaka-akselilla k: Graph, to scale: on the horizontal axis the distance r between the centres of the bodies in metres from zero to ten, on the vertical axis the gravitational force F in micronewtons from zero to 1800, when the mass of each body is 10 tonnes. The points of the falling curve are r = 2 m, F = 1670 µN; r = 4 m, F = 417 µN; r = 6 m, F = 185 µN; r = 8 m, F = 104 µN and r = 10 m, F = 66.7 µN. Dashed lines show that when the distance doubles from two to four metres, the force falls to a quarter.
Kaavakuva, ei mittakaavassa: Maa keskell: Diagram, not to scale: the Earth in the centre. At a distance of two Earth radii from the centre a circle is drawn with a dashed line; from seven points of the circle an orange arrow g of equal length points towards the centre of the Earth. At the right edge of the circle there is a small body on which a red force F = mg acts towards the centre of the Earth.
Kuva, nuolten pituudet mittakaavassa: ne: Picture, arrow lengths to scale: four surfaces side by side, the Moon, Mars, the Earth and Jupiter. Above each surface there is a small sphere and below it an orange arrow whose length is the gravitational field strength, that is, the acceleration due to gravity on the surface: Moon 1.62, Mars 3.71, Earth 9.80 and Jupiter 24.8 metres per second squared.
Kaavakuva kolmessa vaiheessa vasemmalta: Diagram in three stages from left to right, not to scale. First an almost uniform cloud of gas and dust with a slightly denser place. Then the denser places have grown, and arrows show the surrounding matter flowing towards them. Finally a star has formed in the densest place, with a flat disc and small planets orbiting it. Arrows between the stages show the passing of time.
